description: We are Orbit Pulse, a team of second-year BTech Electrical & Electronics Engineering students from NSSCE Palakkad. We're passionate about embedded systems, sensors and electronics, and our challenge is astronaut health monitoring. Our strengths are circuit design, sensor interfacing and hardware prototyping. We're looking for teammates with skills in programming, data analysis, UI design or storytelling who are eager to learn and build something creative.
summary:
Project Orbit Pulse is a real-time health monitoring system for astronauts. It combines wearable sensors that track heart rate, body temperature, and blood oxygen with a dashboard that analyzes the data continuously. Instead of relying on periodic checks, Orbit Pulse learns each astronaut's personal baseline and flags deviations early, so small changes in cardiovascular strain, thermal stress, or fatigue are caught before they become emergencies.
It addresses the challenge by giving both crew and ground teams clear, automatic alerts, which matters most when medical help is far away and communication is delayed. Lightweight, low-power hardware keeps it practical for spacecraft. Orbit Pulse supports safer long-duration missions and also has uses on Earth, such as remote patient care and monitoring in extreme environments.
details: Orbit Pulse is a wearable-based system that monitors an astronaut's vital signs in real time. Sensors measure heart rate, body temperature, and blood oxygen. A microcontroller reads the data and sends it to a dashboard, which compares it against the astronaut's personal baseline and raises color-coded alerts (normal, caution, critical) when readings drift.Early warning of health problems, less dependence on ground-based medical support, continuous data instead of periodic checks, and a simple display that a crew member can understand at a glance.Safer long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars, where help is far away and communication is delayed. The same design can support remote patient care and monitoring in extreme environments on Earth.Sensors for pulse, SpO2, and temperature; a microcontroller for data acquisition; and a software dashboard for visualization and alert logic. Accuracy under microgravity, power and weight limits, comfort during long wear, alert reliability with few false alarms, and scalability for future missions.Instead of fixed thresholds, Orbit Pulse adapts to each individual's baseline, so alerts are personalized. It is also low-cost and low-power, which suits spacecraft constraints.
